curated-agency-lifecycle-stats.businessName: Time to final rule by agency — retained source interpretation
curated-agency-lifecycle-stats.dataGranularityDescription: One agency (or all agencies) and one stratum of rules.
curated-agency-lifecycle-stats.description:
Estimated days to a final rule by agency and stratum, using Aalen–Johansen cumulative incidence with withdrawal as a competing outcome and 95% intervals. Cells pool all proposal years; fewer than 30 rules suppress estimates. NULL quartiles mean the estimate never reaches that probability. Routine families exist only for FAA, EPA and USCG. Each docketed proceeding counts separately, including proposals naming several dockets. Cohort estimates require filtering and recomputing the underlying lifecycles.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-agency-lifecycle-stats.name: curated-agency-lifecycle-stats

properties.name: stratum

properties.name: finals

curated-agenda-item-proceedings.dataGranularityDescription: One evidence record linking one agenda item (RIN) to one proceeding.
curated-agenda-item-proceedings.description:
One row per piece of evidence that an agenda item tracks a proceeding: a docket, Regulations.gov document or Register document that directly reports the RIN for that proceeding. Unified Agenda equality alone never links an action. Keyed `relationship_id`; joins `regulatory_agenda_items` on `agenda_item_id`, `proceedings` on `proceeding_id` and `unified_agenda` on `rin`. Built by `build_regulatory_agenda`; all columns are VARCHAR.

curated-cfr-sections.businessName: Code of Federal Regulations sections — retained source interpretation
curated-cfr-sections.dataGranularityDescription: One GovInfo annual CFR granule: a section, appendix or other structural unit. This is metadata, not regulatory body text. Enclosing parts come from annual volume PART headings, preserving compound and unusual numbering; printed section numbers alone do not identify a part. `cfr_ref` supplies the printed citation. Unchanged or unread volumes can retain earlier placement; the annual index package is excluded. Declared record identity: `granule_id`, `package_id`.
curated-cfr-sections.description:
One GovInfo annual CFR granule: a section, appendix or other structural unit. This is metadata, not regulatory body text. Enclosing parts come from annual volume PART headings, preserving compound and unusual numbering; printed section numbers alone do not identify a part. `cfr_ref` supplies the printed citation. Unchanged or unread volumes can retain earlier placement; the annual index package is excluded.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-cfr-sections.name: curated-cfr-sections

properties.description: GovInfo granule identifier. Primary key / dedup key, including non-section structural units.
properties.name: granule_id

properties.description: GovInfo package identifier for the enclosing annual CFR title and volume.
properties.name: package_id

properties.description: Join key to Federal Register `cfr_references_json`. For a section, the title and its printed citation (e.g. `43-1601.0-1`, `41-50-201.1`); Title 43 keeps its subpart-numbered spelling while `part` names the enclosing part. The Federal Register side cuts every Title 41 compound part at the hyphen (`41 CFR 60-1.4` reads `41-60`), so a Title 41 reference there names a chapter, not a part, and matches no structural row here once the generation carries Title 41's compound parts (see the summary): match it at chapter level (`title = '41' AND part LIKE '60-%'`). NULL for ranges, publisher typos, unprefixed numbers (`Sec. 1-1`), parenthesized citations (`1.401(k)-1`), sections outside a numbered PART and section tokens the volume does not hold; 12 single sections printed with `§§` (`§§ 2.188`) are read as ranges until spicy-docs 0.31.0. For other granules, composed from the part and the identifier's tokens (e.g. `48-700`, `15-746.10-app1`); NULL without a part. A part-level reference (`40-60`) equals `cfr_ref` only on a part's structural rows, of which the part's own granule has `part_granule` `'true'`, and a part held only as sections has none (50 CFR 622 among 12 on 2026-10-03): match a part on `title` and `part`, which section rows carry.
properties.name: cfr_ref

properties.description: CFR title number from the package or granule identifier (e.g. `40`).
properties.name: title

properties.description: For a section, the number in the enclosing PART heading of the package's annual volume XML (e.g. `1600`, `50-201`, `241`); NULL outside a numbered PART or when the volume does not hold the section. For a section's appendix or TOC (`sec746-10-app1`), its host section's part when the volume holds the host, else its token's leading number. For other granules, the identifier's part token including letter suffixes (e.g. `1203a`); in Title 41, whose identifiers cut a compound part at the hyphen, the compound part its part granule's heading states (`60-2`).
properties.name: part

properties.description: For a section, the printed number less its `{part}.` prefix (e.g. `1` for § 50-201.1, `19-8.1` in Part 241, `1601.0-1` in Part 1600, `401(k)-1`). For a section's appendix or TOC, the rest of its token after the leading number (`10-app1`); for a section token the volume does not hold, the whole token. NULL for other granules.
properties.name: section

properties.description: Granule heading / caption text from GovInfo's list-level `title` field.
properties.name: heading

properties.description: GovInfo granule class / structural level (e.g. `CONTENT`, `NODE`, `TOC`, `APPENDIX`).
properties.name: structure_level

properties.description: Annual edition year from the package or granule identifier, falling back to the year in `dateIssued`. This is not necessarily the printed body revision year or proof of a substantive edition.
properties.name: edition_year

properties.description: Granule `lastModified` when supplied, otherwise the enclosing package's `lastModified`. GovInfo's granule listing supplies none, so in practice every row carries its package's stamp.
properties.name: last_modified

properties.description: Canonical GovInfo details URL composed from the package and granule identifiers.
properties.name: url

properties.description: `'true'` on the granule that is a part itself (an id ending `-part200`, or `-part60-id334` in Title 41), `'false'` on every other row. A part's subparts, subject groups, appendices and table of contents share its `cfr_ref` and read `'false'`, so `part_granule = 'true'` picks the part out of them; a part citation's lookup does exactly that. Read from the granule id alone by SpicyDocs' grammar, never from the heading. A part held in two annual editions has one such row per edition, and a part printed across volumes one per volume (40 CFR part 60 spans volumes 7 to 9 of the 2025 edition).
properties.name: part_granule

curated-comment-periods.businessName: Derived submission-date windows — retained source interpretation
curated-comment-periods.dataGranularityDescription: One rule-derived group of source-reported date windows for a notice and its candidate extensions; not a legally adjudicated comment period.
curated-comment-periods.description:
One rule-derived group of source-reported comment windows. Extension/reopening language links windows only when an explicit page citation or qualified RIN uniquely identifies an overlapping or adjoining earlier notice. Conflicts do not link; a gap starts another period. These are candidate groupings, not verified legal extensions. Docket/proceeding anchors never merge groups, and synthetic Federal Register feed dockets anchor none. Ordered source references support navigation.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-comment-periods.name: curated-comment-periods

properties.description: Stable id of the period (`comment_period_<24 hex>`), from the records that open it.
properties.name: comment_period_id

properties.description: JSON array of the proceedings its notices belong to; `[]` when none resolves.
properties.name: proceeding_ids_json

properties.description: JSON array of the RINs its records state and its proceedings hold.
properties.name: rins_json

properties.description: JSON array of the Regulations.gov dockets anchoring it: those its Register record names, else those of its copies, else a Regulations.gov notice's own; never a feed docket. `[]` where the publishers place the notice in no docket (the Register names none and no copy sits in one, as for FCC-2026-2942-0001), which is not proof that none exists.
properties.name: docket_ids_json

properties.description: Eastern day the period opens: the earliest opening among its records (a document's comment start, else its posting; a Register record's publication), `YYYY-MM-DD`.
properties.name: open_date

properties.description: Maximum non-placeholder normalized close among grouped records, YYYY-MM-DD: the later of register_close_date and regulations_gov_close_date. Not a legally controlling/current deadline or a submission-purpose classification. Search all three dates; see data_quality.
properties.name: close_date

properties.description: The sources of the dates it takes, `+`-joined: `documents.comment_end_date` and `federal_register.comments_close_on`.
properties.name: source

properties.description: JSON array of public URLs of the records whose window opens the period on `open_date`.
properties.name: opened_by_artifact_ids_json

properties.description: JSON array of every record in the period, each in exactly one period: dated Register record ids (`number@date`), a notice's Register record included when only its copies state a window, and Regulations.gov document ids.
properties.name: evidence_ids_json

properties.description: How the row was asserted; `deterministic` (computed by rule) throughout.
properties.name: method

properties.description: The builder that asserted the row, with its version (`spicy-regs:comment-periods:v<n>`), bumped when its published rows change.
properties.name: actor_id

properties.description: The materialization run that built the snapshot (e.g. `rulemaking-20260927T062656Z`).
properties.name: run_id

properties.description: When that run asserted the row, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant.
properties.name: asserted_at

properties.description: Id of a prior row this one continues; always NULL here.
properties.name: supersedes_id

properties.description: JSON array of unresolved Register number references attached to its evidence.
properties.name: unresolved_fr_references_json

properties.description: What anchors the period: `docket` when a docket does, `proceeding` when only a proceeding does, `none` when neither; the rulespec export takes the anchored rows.
properties.name: anchor_kind

properties.description: Latest `comments_close_on` of its Register records, `YYYY-MM-DD`; NULL when the Register states none.
properties.name: register_close_date

properties.description: Latest comment end (Eastern day) of its Regulations.gov documents, `YYYY-MM-DD`; NULL when none states one.
properties.name: regulations_gov_close_date

curated-comments.dataGranularityDescription: One posted public-comment record, linked to its stated docket and parent document when those references are supplied. Null docket references remain in the table and agency totals. Attachments, source text and extraction results are separate observations; missing text or file URLs do not prove the publisher received no attachment. Agency-partitioned publication supports scoped record queries.
curated-comments.description:
One posted public-comment record, linked to its stated docket and parent document when those references are supplied. Null docket references remain in the table and agency totals. Attachments, source text and extraction results are separate observations; missing text or file URLs do not prove the publisher received no attachment. Agency-partitioned publication supports scoped record queries.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-comments.name: curated-comments

properties.description: Literal Regulations.gov commentOnDocumentId: the named parent document, independently nullable from docket_id. No identifier-prefix inference. The comment re-read filled it: on receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03) it is set on 26,388,456 of 26,415,400 rows, on at least 98.97% of each of the 12 largest agencies' rows, and below 95% only at MSHA (1,892 of 1,993) and TRAIN (1 of 114). NULL means the record states none or the row was not read; `comment_reference_values_json` tells the two apart. NULL does not mean the comment names no document.
properties.name: comment_on_document_id

properties.description: Literal commentOn in the native object-ID namespace; not interchangeable with a public document key.
properties.name: comment_on_object_id

properties.description: Literal originalDocumentId, retained as an unresolved legacy source reference.
properties.name: original_document_id

properties.description: JSON map containing only present source parent-reference fields, preserving null and empty values. {} means the source was read and fields were absent; SQL NULL means legacy or unread.
properties.name: comment_reference_values_json

properties.description: Unique comment identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
properties.name: comment_id

properties.description: Source-supplied docket identifier for joining to `dockets.docket_id`. Null when the source does not identify a docket; mirror directory names and comment ID prefixes do not fill this field.
properties.name: docket_id

properties.description: Receiving agency's short code.
properties.name: agency_code

properties.description: Commenter's first name, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none or where the row's read did not carry the field; `count(first_name)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
properties.name: first_name

properties.description: Commenter's last name, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none or where the row's read did not carry the field; `count(last_name)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
properties.name: last_name

properties.description: The organization the commenter stated, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none (FDA and EPA state none; EPA classifies submitters in `subtype` instead) and where the row's read did not carry the field. A campaign record carries it where the publisher states it: on receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03) FWS states it on 340 of its 408 `Mass Mail Campaign` and 10 of its 13 `Late Mass Mail Campaign` records, EPA on none of 7,842. `count(organization)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
properties.name: organization

properties.description: Submitter category as regulations.gov states it, where the row's read carried it (FDA's records state one, such as `Individual Consumer` or `Private Industry - C0003`). NULL where the publisher's record states none (EPA states none: it classifies submitters in `subtype` and counts campaigns in `duplicate_comments`) or where the row's read did not carry the field; NULL across a whole agency does not mean the agency does not classify. `count(category)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
properties.name: category

properties.description: Comment title / subject line, as the publisher serves it; a few carry HTML entities (`'`, `&`).
properties.name: title

properties.description:
The comment body as regulations.gov serves it: an HTML fragment, not plain text. Line breaks are `
` tags and many characters are HTML entities (`'`, `"`, `&`, `’`) on many rows of every agency, so a pattern with a plain apostrophe or quotation mark misses them: replace the entities before grouping or quoting. Filled for nearly every comment. Text of attached files is in `text_content`, which is filled only where an attachment was extracted. The largest field in the dataset.
properties.name: comment

properties.description: Document category for the comment record, typically `Public Submission`.
properties.name: document_type

properties.description: When the comment was posted, as the publisher stamps it (ISO 8601 string): a date at Eastern midnight written in UTC (`T04:00:00Z` or `T05:00:00Z`) on most records, a bare date label at `T00:00:00Z` on others. Read the date part as the publisher's date; converting a `T00:00:00Z` label to Eastern moves it a day early.
properties.name: posted_date

properties.description: Timestamp the comment was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
properties.name: modify_date

properties.description: The agency's stated receipt date, stamped as `posted_date` is (ISO 8601 string). It can follow `posted_date` (late or mailed submissions), so compare on the date part.
properties.name: receive_date

properties.description: JSON list of attachment entries in the retained response, including restricted attachments and renditions without a URL. Entries retain `restrictReasonType`/`restrictReason` when stated. NULL means the included set was absent or unavailable in that row; [] means it contained no attachment entries. A format list can be NULL and an individual URL can be NULL. Older rows may retain the earlier filtered representation, so NULL never proves attachment absence.
properties.name: attachments_json

properties.description: Plain text of the comment's attachment(s). Filled inline during the ETL from Mirrulations' own extraction (the bucket's `derived-data` prefix): one extraction tool per comment, its attachments in number order, each stripped and separated by a blank line; when that tool's objects are all blank there is no derived text. Attachments Mirrulations has not extracted are backfilled by the on-demand PDF text-extraction step. Null when neither has produced text; see `text_extraction_status`.
properties.name: text_content

properties.description: Where `text_content` came from, or why there is none. `derived` means Mirrulations' own extraction supplied it (see `pdf_extraction_results_json`); `ok` means Spicy Regs extracted text from at least one PDF, even if another failed; otherwise PDF outcomes prefer `error`, `encrypted`, then `empty`. Derived-data fills written before `derived` existed read `ok` until repaired. Null before an attempt or derived-text fill.
properties.name: text_extraction_status

properties.description: Provenance of `text_content`. For `derived` rows, a JSON object `{comment_id, tool, available_tools, attachments:[{attachment, tool, key, size, etag, sha256}], only_in_other_tools}`: the primary tool (the first of `pypdf`, `pdfminer` with an object for the comment), every tool with an object for it, each attachment's tool, S3 key, listed size and ETag and the SHA-256 of the bytes read (null when the text was kept without re-reading them), and the attachment numbers taken from a tool other than the primary because the primary has no object for them (decision 41); those are in the text. A primary object that exists is kept even when blank. About 125 bytes plus 330 per attachment (31 KB at 92 attachments, the published maximum). Otherwise an ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL; SHA-256 identifies observed bytes, and no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when neither is recorded.
properties.name: pdf_extraction_results_json

properties.description: The agency's own class for the submission (regulations.gov `subtype`), spelled as stated. It is agency-specific. EPA classifies the submitter: `Public Comment` (an individual), `Company/Organization Comment`, `Government Local`, `Government State`, `Government Federal`, `Government Tribal`, `Member of Congress`, `Mass Mail Campaign`, `Late Comment`. Most other agencies that state it put one generic label on every record (`Comment(s)`, `Public Comment`, FDA's `Electronic Regulation from Form`), and many state none. EPA's submitter classes also appear at other agencies in small numbers, and `Mass Mail Campaign` (and `Late Mass Mail Campaign`) at several, FWS among them; which agencies state which labels is a query (`SELECT agency_code, subtype, count(*) … GROUP BY ALL`), not a fixed list. Split organizations from individuals only within an agency that classifies, and not by `organization`: all 1,629 records of EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 leave `organization`, `category` and `first_name` NULL, 219 of them `Company/Organization Comment`. NULL where the record states none or the row predates reading this field.
properties.name: subtype

properties.description: How many received submissions the agency says this posted record stands for (regulations.gov `duplicateComments`), as stated. Agencies that count (EPA and FWS among them) state 1 for a single comment and the campaign's size on a `Mass Mail Campaign` record (15,851 on EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114-1811, National Wildlife Federation Action Fund); agencies that do not count state 0 on every record. Rows are posted records. To estimate submissions, sum `GREATEST(duplicate_comments, 1)`, each posted record standing for at least itself, and first count the NULL rows: GREATEST reads NULL as 1. The sum counts the submissions the agency says its posted records stand for, each record at least itself: its posted accounting, not its official total. On the comments export of receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03), EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114's 1,629 records sum to 53,692, 52,086 of them on its 23 `Mass Mail Campaign` records, while EPA's response to comments reports about 122,200 received. The 2026-09-28 sample found it stated on every record: 0 on 5,281, 1 on 660, more than 1 on 4. NULL where the row predates reading this field; 0 is a stated zero.
properties.name: duplicate_comments

properties.description:
`comment` read as plain text, derived from it each time the mirror is exported and never stored in the catalog. The publisher serves `comment` as an HTML fragment (`I'm`, `
`); this column decodes each character reference once, makes `
` and the end of a block element a newline and a no-break space a space, drops every other tag and trims the ends. Search and quote this column; `comment` keeps the publisher's bytes. The projection loses link targets, list bullets and table layout. One decode only: a body the publisher escaped twice keeps one level (`'` reads `'`), and markup a commenter typed as text (`<br>`) reads as that text. NULL exactly where `comment` is NULL.
properties.name: comment_text

curated-court-opinion-clusters.description:
Decision metadata from CourtListener opinion-clusters bulk data and opinion-search catch-up. cluster_id joins court_opinions.cluster_id (and through it the citation map and parentheticals); cl_docket_id joins court_dockets.cl_docket_id only where both tables hold the same publisher docket object: an appellate decision can name a scraper-created docket while court_dockets holds the RECAP one, so match on the docket number when the id does not join. properties.description: CourtListener opinion-cluster ID: this table's primary/dedup key, one per CourtListener record of a decision, not per decision. The publisher can hold several clusters for one decision, a Supreme Court slip opinion and its later U.S. Reports print above all, and later opinions cite either (Loper Bright: 9986254 and 10600041). Count decisions by `scdb_id`, the publisher's decision key, where it is nonblank. Otherwise group by `cl_docket_id` and reporter citation (court_citations), a heuristic that misses a decision with no reporter citation yet. Supreme Court clusters filed after 2019 had no nonblank `scdb_id` on the 2026-06-30 export; that observation does not establish availability on later exports. Join to court_opinions.cluster_id and court_citations.cluster_id; not an opinion_id.

curated-fec-account-transfers.description:
One source-reported account-transfer or allocated-activity record version. Keeps transferred amounts, activity amounts and totals separate. An account transfer is not automatically a receipt to the reporting committee or a payment to a third party. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row comes from `fec-electronic-filing-schedule`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.

curated-fec-allocation-bases.businessName: Reported allocation basis observations — retained source interpretation
curated-fec-allocation-bases.dataGranularityDescription: One source-reported allocation method, ratio or supporting-basis record version.
curated-fec-allocation-bases.description:
One source-reported allocation method, ratio or supporting-basis record version. Makes source ratios, percentage text, ballot points and supporting amounts inspectable. These are allocation bases and do not create additional payment events. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row comes from `fec-electronic-filing-schedule`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-fec-allocation-bases.name: curated-fec-allocation-bases

curated-fec-committees.description:
One row per observed Federal Election Commission committee. The current reader acquires from the unfiltered OpenFEC `/v1/committees/` endpoint through SpicyDocs; the delivered seed's selected scope is stated above. SpicyRegs preserves the registry's fields, merges complete fresh traversals with prior observations by committee_id, and lets a fresh whole row replace its prior row. Raw page captures and acquisition manifests remain in FEC_CAPTURE_DIR. This identity/reference table can join other records carrying an FEC committee identifier. The company, union or association behind a PAC (FEC's connected organization) is not a column here: join `fec_committee_history` on committee_id and read `connected_organization_name`, one value per two-year cycle as that cycle's committee master states it (take the latest cycle for the current sponsor). first_file_date and last_file_date are dates, cycles and candidate_ids are native lists, and the other columns are text.

One Schedule F expenditure record version. Preserves party authorization roles, candidate, payee, reported amount and accompanying aggregates. Coordinated spending remains distinct from independent spending and receipts. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row has the amount status `exact`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.

curated-fec-disbursements.businessName: Reported disbursement observations — retained source interpretation
curated-fec-disbursements.dataGranularityDescription: One source-reported payment or disbursement record version.
curated-fec-disbursements.description:
One source-reported payment or disbursement record version. Retains payment amount, payee, purpose, codes and memo fields. Refunds, transfers and other source types keep their own meanings; mapping does not select current amendments or a net spending total. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row has the amount status `exact`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-fec-disbursements.name: curated-fec-disbursements

curated-fec-filing-links.description:
One directed native filing reference from a retained filing observation. Follow explicit source references without selecting a latest report. Unknown target resolution, replacement mode and membership completeness remain visible; absence from a partial amendment does not imply deletion. curated-fec-filing-report-observations.description:

curated-fec-filings.description:
One retained metadata observation of a submitted report or statement version. Use record_id for observation identity and nullable filing_key for a proved logical filing version. Group repeated observations by qualified filing identity before reference joins. Linked originals and PDFs retain explicit body status; no current-amendment selection is implied. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. Every row comes from `fec-openfec-file-number`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.

curated-fec-independent-expenditures.businessName: Reported independent-expenditure observations — retained source interpretation
curated-fec-independent-expenditures.description:
One source-reported independent-expenditure record version. Separates spender, payee, candidate target, expenditure date, dissemination date and report metadata. Generic spender_name, payee_name, candidate_name and expenditure_date apply only to layouts that supply those fields. Original-filing Schedule E rows instead retain payee organization/person-name fields, candidate name components, and separate dissemination_date, disbursement_date and signed_date. For an original-filing row, the filing's cover is the fec_filing_report_observations row with the same collection_id and `report_record_role` `reported-form`; its form_type ends N for a new filing and A for an amendment (`F24N`, `F24A`), with source_amendment_date. The header association view (fec_independent_expenditures_filing_associations) finds no filing for any row, original-filing or bulk. These native fields are valid without synthesizing generic names or choosing one date. Target expansion must not multiply the record's full amount; current/net totals need a qualified selection and financial rule. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row has the amount status `exact`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-fec-independent-expenditures.name: curated-fec-independent-expenditures

curated-fec-quality-notices.businessName: Source-issued FEC quality notices — retained source interpretation
curated-fec-quality-notices.dataGranularityDescription: One source notice observation about an explicitly stated filing/committee scope.
curated-fec-quality-notices.description:
One source notice observation about an explicitly stated filing/committee scope. Makes the publisher's warning and linked scope inspectable. A notice does not automatically identify a donor, prove an allegation, resolve an affected transaction, or exclude money from a total. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. Every row comes from `fec-bulk-false-fictitious-notice`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-fec-quality-notices.name: curated-fec-quality-notices

A typo that stays in the range (`26` for `24`) is typed as written and cannot be detected; `first_receipt_date_raw` keeps the date as filed. NULL has its reason in `first_receipt_date_status`; capture time is never substituted.
properties.name: first_receipt_date

curated-fec-receipts.businessName: Campaign money received — retained source interpretation
curated-fec-receipts.dataGranularityDescription: One reported receipt record version or physical source observation.
curated-fec-receipts.description:
One reported receipt record version or physical source observation. Preserves contributor, amount, date, transaction type, memo, source role and evidence. Main/date partitions, amendments and correction streams remain distinct observations; select proved representation membership and a named financial rule before totals. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.

curated-fec-source-records.businessName: Original FEC source records — retained source interpretation
curated-fec-source-records.dataGranularityDescription: One row per provider source record within a selected collection.
curated-fec-source-records.description:
Joinable metadata and retained source evidence across FEC families. collection_id joins fec_collections; source_family joins fec_source_catalog. Rows from different files and election cycles share this table, which has no cycle column: join collection_id to the fec_collection_cycles view for the cycle (2026 means 2025-2026) before comparing with a cycle's totals. A transaction's type, direction, other party, amount and memo flag are fields inside metadata_json (TRANSACTION_TP, OTHER_ID, CAND_ID, TRANSACTION_AMT, MEMO_CD). Native identifiers are lifted only when the provider reports them, and committee_id can join fec_committees. metadata_json and source_record_json preserve the complete provider record. PostgreSQL metadata additionally exposes named_fields from its verified schema; raw COPY fields, decoded NULLs and array text remain separate. Missing IDs remain missing.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-fec-source-records.name: curated-fec-source-records

properties.description: Zero-based source occurrence position within this generation. Repeated source records retain distinct positions; the ordinal is not a stable identity across generations.

In transaction files this is the committee that filed the report, not necessarily the one that received the money: a PAC's contribution to a candidate is filed under the PAC's ID, with the recipient in metadata_json OTHER_ID and CAND_ID, and TRANSACTION_TP says which way the money moved. To find money a committee received from other committees, also search OTHER_ID: in the 2025-2026 file a candidate committee's own filings list no direct PAC contributions, so they appear only under each PAC's committee_id, with the candidate in OTHER_ID and CAND_ID (TRANSACTION_TP 24K). May join fec_committees.committee_id. Blanks remain blank; no identifier is inferred from a name or another entity's ID.

curated-gao-reports.description:
One GAO report or testimony, keyed by product ID. GovInfo, GAO listings/RSS, retained package data and explicit repairs supply records. The table retains earlier observations and fills missing cells; source routes have different periods and metadata. Native `/3` rows expose product URL and source route; earlier schemas retain them in receipts. Major-rule letters provide separate source-stated agency, date and RIN fields, with reading evidence in receipts.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-gao-reports.name: curated-gao-reports

properties.description: GAO product id as gao.gov's product URL spells it (e.g. `gao-26-107974`, `t-rced-94-121`), lowercased. Primary key / dedup key. A GovInfo package id maps to that spelling (`GAOREPORTS-GAO-HEHS-00-73` is `hehs-00-73`, `GAOREPORTS-RCED-AIMD-94-221FS` is `rcedaimd-94-221fs`); a few keep GovInfo's spelling where the package id cannot recover gao.gov's.
properties.name: report_id

properties.description: Product title as the route states it; on a listing row, the teaser's label and heading joined as `label: heading`, which is how the feed titles the same products. The Month in Review cuts a long heading at about 200 characters and ends it `...`; where GAO's major-rule listing states that heading whole, the title is whole. A `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row's is `Federal Agency Major Rule Report: ` and the heading GAO's listing or the report's product page states, or the heading alone on the AIMD- and GGD- products. A few GovInfo titles are GovInfo's placeholder `GAO Report from` and the number. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. GAO double-escapes some headings, so a few listing titles keep `—`, `—` or `&` literally, as GAO's page displays them; apply `html.unescape` when matching.
properties.name: title

properties.description: GAO product type. The feed tags no finer type, so a feed or upstream-copied row is `Report`; a GovInfo or listing row is `Testimony` for a `T-` number or a number ending in `T`, else `Report`; NULL on a report added by explicit repair.
properties.name: report_type

properties.description: Publication date as an ISO date string (e.g. `2026-07-17`): the feed's `pubDate` (upstream's feed for a copied row), GovInfo's `dateIssued`, the listing's "Publicly Released" date (its "Published" date where it states no release), GAO's issue date on a `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row (those listings state no release date), or the day a repaired product's page states. Sort key.
properties.name: published_date

properties.description: The product summary: the feed's (GAO's `What GAO Found` / `Why GAO Did This Study` narrative), or a GovInfo row's MODS `abstract` with whitespace runs collapsed; NULL where neither states one, and on repair and listing rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.
properties.name: abstract

properties.description: Reserved JSON array of agencies the product covers. The RSS feed carries no structured agency tags, so this is `[]` pending a future enrichment source; NULL on repair, GovInfo (MODS names no agency) and listing rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.
properties.name: agencies_json

properties.description: JSON array of topics. A GovInfo row's is its MODS `subject/topic` terms in the record's order, GAO's own index terms, program names and places, kept as stated (a long name can arrive split in two); NULL where the MODS states none or is unread. A listing row's is GAO's own topic headings the product was listed under, as GAO spells them and in listed order; a `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row's is NULL, since those listings state no topic. The RSS feed carries no topic tags, so a feed or upstream-copied row is `[]`; NULL on repair rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.
properties.name: topics_json

properties.description: The product's page on the route that supplied the row: the gao.gov product page for feed, upstream-copied, repair and every listing's rows, GovInfo's details page (composed from the package id) for GovInfo rows.
properties.name: url

properties.description: The route that supplied the row: `gao_rss` (the daily feed), `upstream_copy` (copied once from upstream spicy-regs' published table), `gao_repair` (an explicit single-report repair), `govinfo` (GovInfo's GAOREPORTS listing), `gao_listing` (GAO's own Month in Review and Annual Index), `gao_major_rule_listing` (GAO's Congressional Review Act listing, "Reports on Major Rules"), `gao_major_rule_index` (GAO's index of 2000-12-15 of its 1996-2000 major-rule reports, and each report's product page) or `gao_r_package` (copied once from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package by Jack T. Rametta, GPL-3.0-or-later).
properties.name: source

properties.description: The publisher's product type, finer than `report_type`, which keeps its values. A GovInfo row's is its MODS type (e.g. `Letter Report`, `Correspondence`, `Testimony`, `Fact Sheet`, `Other Written Product`). A listing row has one only where GAO's teaser shows a finer type in place of a subject (`Federal Agency Major Rule Report`, on every major-rule report; `Correspondence`; `Other Written Product`); NULL where it shows a subject or only `Report`/`Testimony`. A report GAO's major-rule listings state is `Federal Agency Major Rule Report` on their word, whatever route holds its row: every `gao_major_rule_listing` and `gao_major_rule_index` row but the AIMD- and GGD- products that listing also states (NULL), and the few GovInfo rows those listings name, GAO-01-1024R among them though it reports on no rule (GAO lists it so; owner decision 2026-10-04). NULL on other routes and on unread GovInfo rows.
properties.name: product_type

properties.description: The report number as the route prints it, the form other documents cite and users search for: a GovInfo row's MODS (e.g. `GAO-08-919R`, `RCED/AIMD-94-221FS`, `GAO/HEHS-00-73`) or the product number on GAO's listing page (e.g. `GAO-26-108426`, `OGC-96-9` for a major-rule report of 1996 to 2000, or `B-331093` for one from April 2017 on). The listing fills it on any row it lists whose number is NULL, whatever route supplied the row, and never replaces one. NULL on other feed, upstream-copied and repair rows, and on GovInfo rows whose MODS is unread. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.
properties.name: report_number

properties.description: Why GAO did the work, as the R package states it: `congressional_request`, `testimony`, `correspondence`, `cg_initiated` (the Comptroller General's own initiative) or `statutory_mandate`. NULL where the package states none, and on reports issued after its copy (2026-09-26) until a GAO product-page reader fills them.
properties.name: requester_type

properties.description: JSON array of the requesting congressional committees, as the R package extracted them from the report (e.g. `Committee on Armed Services (Senate)`). NULL where it states none, and on reports issued after its copy.
properties.name: requester_committees_json

properties.description: JSON array of the requesting members of Congress, as the R package extracted them from the report's text, with its OCR errors kept (e.g. `Charles H. Percy (Senate)`). NULL where it states none, and on reports issued after its copy.
properties.name: requester_members_json

properties.description: How many recommendations the product makes (0 for none): the rows of "Recommendations for Executive Action" on the report's GAO product page where a page read has set it, else the R package's count. BIGINT. NULL on reports the package does not list and no page read has reached.
properties.name: recommendation_count

properties.description: How many matters for congressional consideration the product raises (0 for none): the rows of "Matter for Congressional Consideration" on the report's GAO product page where a page read has set it, else the R package's count. BIGINT. NULL on reports the package does not list and no page read has reached.
properties.name: matters_for_congress_count

properties.description: The report's page count: the pages GAO's product page states for the file it labels Full Report where a page read has set it, else the R package's. BIGINT. NULL where neither states one.
properties.name: page_count

properties.description: JSON array of GAO's subject index terms for the product (e.g. `Cost control`, `Financial management`), finer than `topics_json`: the terms the report's GAO product page lists, as GAO spells them and in page order, where a page read has set it, else the R package's. GAO retags products, so the two can differ. NULL where neither states any.
properties.name: subject_terms_json

properties.description: The agency that issued the rule a Federal Agency Major Rule Report is on, as the report's letter prints it in its opening sentence (e.g. `Department of Health and Human Services, Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA)`): one string in GAO's wording, abbreviations kept, the agencies of a joint rule in one clause and not split. It is not an agency key, and GAO spells one agency several ways. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report, on one whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states no such clause.
properties.name: major_rule_agency

properties.description: JSON array of every Regulation Identifier Number the letter of a Federal Agency Major Rule Report states for the rule or rules the report is on, each as `NNNN-LLNN` (e.g. `2040-AB75`), in the letter's order. The join key to `unified_agenda.rin` and to the entries of `federal_register.regulation_id_numbers`. The list is not paired with `major_rule_fr_citations_json`: entry k of one is not the RIN of entry k of the other, and a report on two rules often states one RIN for both, so take a rule's RIN beside its citation from `federal_register`. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report or whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states none in that form: it names a docket, an FCC number or a ZRIN instead, or GAO mistyped it.
properties.name: major_rule_rins_json

properties.description: JSON array of the Federal Register citation of each rule a Federal Agency Major Rule Report is on, as its letter states it, each as `{volume}-{page}` (`66-6976` for 66 Fed. Reg. 6976), in the letter's order: one for most reports, several where a report is on several rules or on a rule published as several documents. Each joins `federal_register` on `volume` and `start_page` (`split_part(c, '-', 1) = volume AND split_part(c, '-', 2) = start_page`); a few letters cite the page before the document starts or a page inside it. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report or whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states no citation: the rule was not published in the Federal Register, or the letter's opening cites none.

curated-lobbying-filings.businessName: Lobbying disclosure filings — retained source interpretation
curated-lobbying-filings.dataGranularityDescription: One row per federal lobbying-disclosure filing, ingested from the U.S. Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) REST API (`lda.gov`, formerly `lda.senate.gov`) by `build_lobbying_filings`. Registrants file quarterly reports naming the clients they lobby for, the money involved, the issues raised, and the government entities (agencies/chambers) lobbied — so this table links the comment campaigns in `comments`/`dockets` to the same organizations' *direct* agency lobbying. Primary / dedup key is `filing_uuid`. Declared record identity: `filing_uuid`.
curated-lobbying-filings.description:
One row per federal lobbying-disclosure filing, ingested from the U.S. Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) REST API (`lda.gov`, formerly `lda.senate.gov`) by `build_lobbying_filings`. Registrants file quarterly reports naming the clients they lobby for, the money involved, the issues raised, and the government entities (agencies/chambers) lobbied — so this table links the comment campaigns in `comments`/`dockets` to the same organizations' *direct* agency lobbying. Primary / dedup key is `filing_uuid`.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-lobbying-filings.name: curated-lobbying-filings

properties.description: LDA filing UUID (e.g. `7866327b-c892-4430-b9f0-1f0f679c58c6`). Primary key / dedup key.
properties.name: filing_uuid

properties.description: The LDA filing-type code as the API states it: `RR` registration; `Q1`–`Q4` quarterly reports and `MM` the pre-2008 mid-year report; `1A`–`4A` and `MA` amendments; `1T`–`4T` and `MT` terminations; `1@`–`4@` and `M@` termination amendments; a trailing `Y` marks a no-activity report (`Q1Y`, `1@Y`). The LDA constants endpoint (`/api/v1/constants/filing/filingtypes/`) is the authority. An amendment is a separate filing that restates its quarter's report. To total amounts, drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`), which carry a `filing_period` too, then keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and period: with registrations kept, a later one displaced a quarterly report in 103 groups of 2025 (measured 2026-10-03). For issues or activities, choose filing types first: a termination chain (`1T`, then a no-activity `1@Y`) shares the period, and the latest filing can be the no-activity one.
properties.name: filing_type

properties.description: Calendar year the filing reports on.
properties.name: filing_year

properties.description: Reporting period within the year (e.g. `first_quarter`, `year_end`).
properties.name: filing_period

properties.description: Timestamp the filing was posted to the LDA system (ISO 8601 string with timezone). Sort key.
properties.name: dt_posted

properties.description: Name of the registrant (the lobbying firm or self-filing organization).
properties.name: registrant_name

properties.description: LDA registrant id. Stable join key across a registrant's filings.
properties.name: registrant_id

properties.description: The client's name as the registrant filed it; a name, not an identity. A self-filing organization is both registrant and client, often under a spelling other registrants do not use for it (McKesson files as `MCKESSON CORPORATION & AFFILIATES …`). `registrant_id` keys the registrant across its filings and `client_id` keys a client only within one registrant (see `client_id`); a match to `comments.organization` or `sam_entities.legal_business_name` is a name match.
properties.name: client_name

properties.description: LDA's `client.id`: one registrant's record of one client, stable across that registrant's filings, not an organization identity. No id is shared between registrants (129,434 ids for 129,434 registrant-client pairs, measured 2026-10-03), so an organization hired by several firms has one id per firm (AT&T Services, Inc.: 21 ids under 21 registrants in 2025).
properties.name: client_id

properties.description: Lobbying income reported by a lobbying firm for the period, in USD. Null for self-filers (who report `expenses`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`) and keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and quarter (see `filing_type`).
properties.name: income

properties.description: Lobbying expenses reported by a self-filing organization for the period, in USD. Null for firms (who report `income`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`) and keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and quarter (see `filing_type`). A self-filing organization's expenses already include what it pays outside lobbying firms, whose `income` for that client is reported separately; do not add the two.
properties.name: expenses

properties.description: JSON array of lobbying activities, each `{general_issue_code, general_issue_code_display, description}` — the issue areas lobbied and their free-text descriptions.
properties.name: lobbying_activities_json

properties.description: JSON array of the distinct government entities lobbied (`{id, name}`) — the agencies and chambers (e.g. `HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES`, `SENATE`) named across the filing's activities.
properties.name: government_entities_json

properties.description: URL of the filing's printable document page on lda.gov (`filing_document_url`; lda.senate.gov redirects there).
properties.name: url

properties.description: The publisher's label for `filing_type`, as served (e.g. `1st Quarter - Report`, `Registration`).
properties.name: filing_type_display

properties.description: The publisher's label for `filing_period`, as served (e.g. `1st Quarter (Jan 1 - Mar 31)`).
properties.name: filing_period_display

properties.description: Media type of the filing document (the receipt's `url`), as LDA states it (e.g. `text/html`, `application/pdf`); null on the few filings that state none.
properties.name: filing_document_content_type

properties.description: The self-filer's expense accounting method code as filed (`expenses_method`). Two spellings occur, both kept as filed: lower case `a`, `b`, `c`, whose `expenses_method_display` is the long label, and upper case `A`, `B`, `C`, whose display is the bare letter; both occur in current years (a 400-page retained sample, 2026-10-30, held 751 lower-case and 286 upper-case codes). `a`/`A` is Method A (LDA definitions), `b`/`B` Method B (IRC 6033(b)(8)), `c`/`C` Method C (IRC 162(e)). Null when the filing states no method, as on most firm reports, which carry `income` instead.
properties.name: expenses_method

properties.description: The publisher's label for `expenses_method`, as filed: `Method A - Reporting amounts using LDA definitions only`, `Method B - Reporting amounts under section 6033(b)(8) of the Internal Revenue Code`, `Method C - Reporting amounts under section 162(e) of the Internal Revenue Code`, or the bare letter when the code is upper case.
properties.name: expenses_method_display

properties.description: Date the registrant ended its representation of the client, on a termination report (`filing_type` `1T`–`4T`, `MT` and their no-activity forms). Null on other filings.
properties.name: termination_date

properties.description: Name of the person who signed and posted the filing, as entered (often with a title, e.g. `Frank J. Donatelli, Senior Advisor`).
properties.name: posted_by_name

properties.description: First line of the registrant's address as filed on this filing. The address can differ between a registrant's filings; it is the filing's own, not a current registrant profile.
properties.name: registrant_address_1

properties.description: Second line of the registrant's address as filed on this filing; null when none was filed.
properties.name: registrant_address_2

properties.description: City of the registrant's address as filed on this filing.
properties.name: registrant_city

properties.description: State code of the registrant's address as filed on this filing (e.g. `DC`); null for an address outside the United States.
properties.name: registrant_state

properties.description: ZIP or postal code of the registrant's address as filed on this filing.
properties.name: registrant_zip

properties.description: Country of the registrant's address as filed on this filing, as the publisher displays it (e.g. `United States of America`), not a country code.
properties.name: registrant_country

properties.description: Country of the registrant's principal place of business as filed, when the filing states one (display name); null otherwise.
properties.name: registrant_ppb_country

properties.description: The filing's flag for whether the registrant's principal place of business differs from the address filed: true, false, or null when the filing does not carry it (registrations among others).
properties.name: registrant_different_address

curated-org-committee-links.businessName: Commenter organizations matched to committees — retained source interpretation
curated-org-committee-links.dataGranularityDescription: One row per commenter organization name and FEC committee name match.
curated-org-committee-links.description:
One row per (commenter organization name, FEC committee) name match, derived by `build_org_committee_links`. Materializes the organization-name bridge between the regulations.gov corpus and `fec_committees` — the join the data model always described but left to each query author, so every consumer normalized names differently. `organization` is the raw string as filed, joining straight back to `comments.organization`; `committee_id` joins to `fec_committees`. Coverage is inherently small: `comments.organization` is stated on a small share of comments (`count(organization)` over `comments` is the measure) and on none at some agencies (FDA, EPA), and most commenting organizations do not run a federal PAC, so most organization names matching no committee is the expected outcome rather than a matcher to tune harder. Matching runs in three tiers (`exact`, `core`, `prefix`) and every row carries `match_method`, `confidence`, and `committee_match_count` so consumers pick their own precision bar instead of trusting an opaque score. A high `committee_match_count` can reflect multiple committees sharing a name prefix; inspect the source evidence before treating those matches as an affiliation network. The comment counts and dates on a row cover every agency and year the comments table holds and repeat on each committee row of the same organization string.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-org-committee-links.name: curated-org-committee-links

properties.description: Commenter organization exactly as filed on the comment. Join key back to `comments.organization`.
properties.name: organization

properties.description: `organization` uppercased with parenthetical asides, apostrophes and punctuation removed and `&` expanded to `AND`.
properties.name: organization_norm

properties.description: `organization_norm` with trailing legal suffixes (`INC`, `LLC`, ...) and a leading `THE` removed. The form the `core`/`prefix` tiers compare.
properties.name: organization_core

properties.description: Where the organization name came from. Always `organization_field` today; text-derived names (comment title, letterhead, signature block) would be added as extra rows under their own source.
properties.name: name_source

properties.description: Matched OpenFEC committee identifier. Joins to `fec_committees.committee_id`, whose `filing_frequency` (`T` or `A`: terminated) and `last_file_date` say whether the committee still files.
properties.name: committee_id

properties.description: Matched committee name as registered with the FEC.
properties.name: committee_name

properties.description: Human-readable committee type of the matched committee (e.g. `PAC - Qualified`). Never a House, Senate or presidential candidate's committee: those links are left out.
properties.name: committee_type_full

properties.description: Human-readable committee designation of the matched committee. Never `Leadership PAC`: those links are left out.
properties.name: designation_full

properties.description: Human-readable political party of the matched committee. Often null for non-party committees.
properties.name: party_full

properties.description: Sponsoring organization type of the matched committee (e.g. `Trade Association`, `Labor Organization`). Often null.
properties.name: organization_type_full

properties.description: Two-letter state on the matched committee (`fec_committees.state`). Often null.
properties.name: committee_state

properties.description: How the pair matched: `exact` (full normalized names equal), `core` (decoration-stripped cores equal), or `prefix` (committee core starts with the whole organization core on a token boundary).
properties.name: match_method

properties.description: `high` for `exact`/`core`; for `prefix`, `medium` when `committee_match_count` <= 5 and `low` above that. Grades the name match alone: it ignores whether the committee still files and the sponsor FEC states (`sponsor_name_match`). Filter on this to pick a precision bar.
properties.name: confidence

properties.description: How many FEC committees this organization name matched in total, counting the candidate committees and leadership PACs whose links are left out, so it can exceed this string's rows here. A high count does not establish an affiliate network; inspect source evidence alongside the matching rule.
properties.name: committee_match_count

properties.description: Comments filed under this exact organization string in every agency and year the comments table holds (deduplicated on `comment_id`, newest `modify_date` wins — matching the MCP `comments` view). The same value repeats on each committee row of the string; do not sum it across rows.
properties.name: comment_count

properties.description: Distinct dockets this organization string commented on, across every agency and year. Repeats on each committee row of the string.
properties.name: docket_count

properties.description: JSON array of the distinct agency codes this organization commented to, across every year, sorted. Repeats on each committee row of the string.
properties.name: agency_codes_json

properties.description: Earliest `posted_date` across this organization's comments in every agency and year (ISO 8601 string).
properties.name: first_comment_date

properties.description: Latest `posted_date` across this organization's comments in every agency and year (ISO 8601 string).
properties.name: last_comment_date

properties.description: The committee's connected organization (its sponsor) as FEC states it, verbatim from `fec_committee_history.connected_organization_name` in the latest filing year that names one. NULL when no year names one: FEC's placeholders (`NONE`, `N/A`, `NA`, `BLANK`, `0`, punctuation alone), which that table keeps verbatim, are read as naming none. Filers sometimes write the PAC's own name, a former name or a parent company here.
properties.name: connected_organization_name

properties.description: Whether `connected_organization_name` names the commenting organization: `agrees` when it reduces to `organization_core` under the same normalization (read also with PAC words such as `POLITICAL ACTION COMMITTEE` removed, spaces ignored); `differs` otherwise, most often the same organization spelled another way (`ASSN`, inverted words, a typo), a former name or a parent company, sometimes a different sponsor; `not_stated` when FEC names no sponsor. A name comparison, not an identity.
properties.name: sponsor_name_match

curated-proceedings.dataGranularityDescription: One rulemaking proceeding: the dockets and Register documents that are one action.
curated-proceedings.description:
One rulemaking proceeding with its source dockets, Register documents and staged events. RINs provide agenda evidence and never merge dockets. Withdrawn Regulations.gov postings supply no event, title, agency or RIN evidence. A docket-less proceeding is one Register document. `proceeding_id` continues across generations when source records overlap; main IDs link agenda associations, comment periods and lifecycle records.

Definition purpose: retained source interpretation. Meaning for source/processing fields the maintained producer keeps in receipts; not an admitted table version.
curated-proceedings.name: curated-proceedings

properties.description: Stable opaque id of the proceeding (`proceeding_<24 hex>`), continued from the prior generation where it overlaps one.
properties.name: proceeding_id

properties.description: The proceeding's RIN when it holds exactly one, else NULL; a query aid, never its identity (`rins_json` lists every RIN).
properties.name: rin

properties.description: JSON array of the Regulations.gov dockets the proceeding comprises; `[]` for a docket-less proceeding.
properties.name: docket_ids_json

properties.description: Title of its most recently dated titled document.
properties.name: title

properties.description: The agency code most of its documents carry. A docket-less proceeding takes its Register document's agency code. Each Register agency maps to one Regulations.gov code through RefSpec's agency projection and agency registry, whose identity bridges and successions give a defunct agency its current successor's code whatever the document's date: a 1998 Health Care Finance Administration notice is CMS. A split agency maps only when every successor gives the same one code. A department named with one of its own agencies yields to it (Transportation Department with FAA is FAA), and a department signing with one of its own unmapped bureaus keeps the department's code. NULL when no agency maps or the agencies are unrelated.
properties.name: agency_code

properties.description: The one stage (`proposed`, `supplemental`, `final` or `withdrawn`) of its latest dated events; NULL when none, or when that day's events disagree.

properties.description: JSON array of its stage events, one per staged document: `{effective_date, event_kind, evidence_id, joined_by, source, stage}`.

properties.description: JSON array of the Federal Register document numbers it holds.
properties.name: fr_document_numbers_json

properties.description: JSON array of the CFR references (`title-part`) that the `rule_targets` edges of its dockets name.
properties.name: cfr_refs_json

properties.description: The same CFR references as Rulespec identifiers (e.g. `urn:rkaf:us:cfr:40:60`).
properties.name: cfr_target_iris_json

properties.description: Always `[]`: legal authority belongs to the editioned Unified Agenda entry, never to an action.
properties.name: authority_refs_json

properties.description: How the row was asserted; `deterministic` (computed by rule) throughout.
properties.name: method

properties.description: The builder that asserted the row, with its version (`spicy-regs:proceedings:v<n>`), bumped when its published rows change.
properties.name: actor_id

properties.description: The materialization run that built the snapshot (e.g. `rulemaking-20260927T062656Z`).
properties.name: run_id

properties.description: When that run asserted the row, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant.
properties.name: asserted_at

properties.description: The prior generation's `proceeding_id` this proceeding continues, so equal to `proceeding_id` on a continuing row (the id carries over); NULL for a proceeding new in this generation.
properties.name: supersedes_id

properties.description: JSON array of the dated Federal Register record ids (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`) it holds.
properties.name: fr_document_ids_json

properties.description: How each `fr_document_ids_json` document joined, in the same order: `{fr_document_id, joined_by}`, `joined_by` being `fr_docket_link`, `fr_copy`, `specific_rin` or `fr_document`.
properties.name: fr_document_joins_json

properties.description: JSON array of Register number references it holds that resolve to no single record, each with its candidates and status.
properties.name: unresolved_fr_references_json

properties.description: JSON array of every RIN it holds, from its dockets, documents and Register documents.
properties.name: rins_json

One observed link between a Regulations.gov docket, a CFR part or a Unified Agenda RIN, with its source evidence class. Missing and ambiguous references remain unresolved. Action-notice citation rows can have both targets NULL. RIN navigation returns agenda editions; it does not merge proceedings. Main identifiers carry the relationship; receipts retain interpretation evidence.

current-agency-lifecycle-stats.dataGranularityDescription: One agency (or all agencies) and one stratum of rules.
current-agency-lifecycle-stats.description:
Estimated days to a final rule by agency and stratum, using Aalen–Johansen cumulative incidence with withdrawal as a competing outcome and 95% intervals. Cells pool all proposal years; fewer than 30 rules suppress estimates. NULL quartiles mean the estimate never reaches that probability. Routine families exist only for FAA, EPA and USCG. Each docketed proceeding counts separately, including proposals naming several dockets. Cohort estimates require filtering and recomputing the underlying lifecycles.

Definition purpose: native output definition. Independent writer declaration checked; no data version implied.

current-cfr-sections.dataGranularityDescription: One GovInfo annual CFR granule: a section, appendix or other structural unit. This is metadata, not regulatory body text. Enclosing parts come from annual volume PART headings, preserving compound and unusual numbering; printed section numbers alone do not identify a part. `cfr_ref` supplies the printed citation. current-cfr-sections.description:
One GovInfo annual CFR granule: a section, appendix or other structural unit. This is metadata, not regulatory body text. Enclosing parts come from annual volume PART headings, preserving compound and unusual numbering; printed section numbers alone do not identify a part. `cfr_ref` supplies the printed citation. Unchanged or unread volumes can retain earlier placement; the annual index package is excluded.

Definition purpose: native output definition. Independent writer declaration checked; no data version implied.
current-cfr-sections.name: current-cfr-sections

properties.description: GovInfo granule identifier. Primary key / dedup key, including non-section structural units.
properties.name: granule_id

properties.description: `'true'` on the granule that is a part itself (an id ending `-part200`, or `-part60-id334` in Title 41), `'false'` on every other row. A part's subparts, subject groups, appendices and table of contents share its `cfr_ref` and read `'false'`, so `part_granule = 'true'` picks the part out of them; a part citation's lookup does exactly that. Read from the granule id alone by SpicyDocs' grammar, never from the heading. A part held in two annual editions has one such row per edition, and a part printed across volumes one per volume (40 CFR part 60 spans volumes 7 to 9 of the 2025 edition).
properties.name: part_granule

properties.description: GovInfo package identifier for the enclosing annual CFR title and volume.
properties.name: package_id

properties.description: Join key to Federal Register `cfr_references`. For a section, the title and its printed citation (e.g. `43-1601.0-1`, `41-50-201.1`); Title 43 keeps its subpart-numbered spelling while `part` names the enclosing part. The Federal Register side cuts every Title 41 compound part at the hyphen (`41 CFR 60-1.4` reads `41-60`), so a Title 41 reference there names a chapter, not a part, and matches no structural row here once the generation carries Title 41's compound parts (see the summary): match it at chapter level (`title = '41' AND part LIKE '60-%'`). NULL for ranges, publisher typos, unprefixed numbers (`Sec. 1-1`), parenthesized citations (`1.401(k)-1`), sections outside a numbered PART and section tokens the volume does not hold; 12 single sections printed with `§§` (`§§ 2.188`) are read as ranges until spicy-docs 0.31.0. For other granules, composed from the part and the identifier's tokens (e.g. `48-700`, `15-746.10-app1`); NULL without a part. A part-level reference (`40-60`) equals `cfr_ref` only on a part's structural rows, of which the part's own granule has `part_granule` `'true'`, and a part held only as sections has none (50 CFR 622 among 12 on 2026-10-03): match a part on `title` and `part`, which section rows carry.
properties.name: cfr_ref

properties.description: CFR title number from the package or granule identifier (e.g. `40`).
properties.name: title

properties.description: For a section, the number in the enclosing PART heading of the package's annual volume XML (e.g. `1600`, `50-201`, `241`); NULL outside a numbered PART or when the volume does not hold the section. For a section's appendix or TOC (`sec746-10-app1`), its host section's part when the volume holds the host, else its token's leading number. For other granules, the identifier's part token including letter suffixes (e.g. `1203a`); in Title 41, whose identifiers cut a compound part at the hyphen, the compound part its part granule's heading states (`60-2`).
properties.name: part

properties.description: For a section, the printed number less its `{part}.` prefix (e.g. `1` for § 50-201.1, `19-8.1` in Part 241, `1601.0-1` in Part 1600, `401(k)-1`). For a section's appendix or TOC, the rest of its token after the leading number (`10-app1`); for a section token the volume does not hold, the whole token. NULL for other granules.
properties.name: section

Attachments Mirrulations has not extracted are backfilled by the on-demand PDF text-extraction step. Null when neither has produced text; see `text_extraction_status`.

properties.description: Where `text_content` came from, or why there is none. `derived` means Mirrulations' own extraction supplied it (see `pdf_extraction_results_json`); `ok` means Spicy Regs extracted text from at least one PDF, even if another failed; otherwise PDF outcomes prefer `error`, `encrypted`, then `empty`. Derived-data fills written before `derived` existed read `ok` until repaired. Null before an attempt or derived-text fill.
properties.name: text_extraction_status

properties.description: Provenance of `text_content`. For `derived` rows, a JSON object `{comment_id, tool, available_tools, attachments:[{attachment, tool, key, size, etag, sha256}], only_in_other_tools}`: the primary tool (the first of `pypdf`, `pdfminer` with an object for the comment), every tool with an object for it, each attachment's tool, S3 key, listed size and ETag and the SHA-256 of the bytes read (null when the text was kept without re-reading them), and the attachment numbers taken from a tool other than the primary because the primary has no object for them (decision 41); those are in the text. A primary object that exists is kept even when blank. About 125 bytes plus 330 per attachment (31 KB at 92 attachments, the published maximum). Otherwise an ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL; SHA-256 identifies observed bytes, and no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when neither is recorded.
